cards.script: On a GLP-1, the harder you push your colon
cards.label: Recognizable MiraLAX, magnesium and fiber packages dominate the foreground against a dark navy anatomical backdrop. The connected digestive tract is visible behind them, not inside a product package.

cards.script: with laxatives and fiber, the more stuck you can feel.
cards.label: Same coherent digestive-tract illustration, framed to include both colon and stomach. A restrained locator highlights the colon; the stomach remains visible above it.

cards.script: Here’s the trap no one explains.
cards.label: Same woman seated on the closed toilet lid, clothed in a grey cotton tee and lounge trousers; she looks from the counter to her abdomen. Tighten framing with a hard cut.

cards.script: Your GLP-1 slows your stomach down.
cards.label: Whole digestive tract; amber highlight stays on the anatomically correct stomach. Slow, subtle movement rather than a frozen or sealed organ.

cards.script: So when you haven’t gone in days,
cards.label: Same woman sits on the edge of the bathtub, fully clothed, elbows resting on thighs. She exhales and looks down.

cards.script: you reach for MiraLAX, magnesium, stool softeners, or more fiber.
cards.label: Four quick object reveals on the counter, one per named remedy. Use real package references; allow internal picture changes on each product name.

cards.script: Those products work downstream. They target the colon—
cards.label: Torso diagram: camera travels down the continuous digestive tract and highlights the colon. Keep the stomach visible in the same diagram.

cards.script: the end of your digestive system.
cards.label: Closer view of the colon in the same diagram. A simple editor-set COLON label lands beside it; no empty-tube claim.

cards.script: But if the slowdown begins higher up in your stomach,
cards.label: Hard cut back to the upper torso. Highlight the stomach at the exact word stomach; the entire tract remains connected.

cards.script: food is still sitting at the beginning.
cards.label: Stomach cross-section shows a modest meal and gradual mixing; no solid brick, stool, complete obstruction, or food packed into the esophagus.

cards.script: That’s why the relief may last a day,
cards.label: Same woman looks briefly hopeful at her bathroom mirror, then cut to her returning to the counter the following morning.

cards.script: the fiber can make you feel even fuller,
cards.label: Side-on seated portrait at breakfast; woman gently loosens her waistband and leaves the bowl partly eaten. Subtle fullness, no extreme distension.

cards.script: and those rotten-egg burps keep coming back.
cards.label: Same woman at the dining table brings a closed hand to her mouth and turns away discreetly. Avoid a cartoon gas cloud.

cards.script: It’s not that your body is broken.
cards.label: Eye-level close portrait. She relaxes her shoulders slightly, still thoughtful. Hold long enough for the reassurance to land.

cards.script: And it doesn’t mean you have to quit your shot.
cards.label: Her hand sets the correctly referenced medication pen beside its box. Do not show injection technique or throw medication away.

cards.script: You’ve been trying to solve an upstream slowdown with downstream tools.
cards.label: One full-frame anatomy map. Two editor-set callouts read STOMACH / UPSTREAM and COLON / DOWNSTREAM. Alternate emphasis between them.

cards.script: What you need is something designed to wake your stomach back up
cards.label: Stay on the neutral stomach map. A soft highlight introduces the proposed movement-support job. No switch flipping, nerve repair, or restart demonstration.

cards.script: while supporting everything below it.
cards.label: Camera moves down the same connected tract; a second quiet highlight joins the first. Keep the diagram visually continuous.

cards.script: And to do that, you need three specific things.
cards.label: Three clean numbered ingredient spaces fill the frame. Show 1, 2, 3; no product bottle or Motilli mark yet.

cards.script: First, apigenin—a plant compound concentrated from celery juice—
cards.label: Macro of washed celery stalks and a small glass of green juice on cream stone. Editor-set APIGENIN / FROM CELERY label; first checklist dot fills.

cards.script: to support your stomach’s natural wave-like movement.
cards.label: Neutral illustrative stomach with an external wave line indicating the intended job. No causal before/after animation showing celery restarting contractions.

cards.script: Second, a low-viscosity soluble fiber
cards.label: Fine soluble fiber ingredient in a glass dish beside water. Editor-set SOLUBLE PREBIOTIC FIBER label; second checklist dot fills.

cards.script: that holds water in the stool
cards.label: Restrained diagram of water and stool inside the colon; label this an illustrative concept. Do not show FOS behaving as a proven gel-forming osmotic agent.

cards.script: without becoming another heavy bulk load.
cards.label: Small measured ingredient dish beside the actual referenced full-size fiber container. No fabricated gram numbers or zero-bulk comparison graphic.

cards.script: And third, chlorophyllin to neutralize the sulfur compounds
cards.label: Deep-green chlorophyllin ingredient material in a laboratory-style glass dish, editor-set CHLOROPHYLLIN label; third checklist dot fills. No fabricated molecular binding.

cards.script: behind those burps instead of merely covering the smell.
cards.label: Return to the dining scene as the woman sets down a mint packet. Stay neutral; do not portray the ingredient producing instant relief.

cards.script: That’s why Motilli combines all three
cards.label: FIRST MOTILLI REVEAL: the verified current bottle enters between the three ingredient dishes. Label faces the lens and remains readable.

cards.script: in two heart-shaped gummies made specifically for people on GLP-1s.
cards.label: Macro of exactly two dark-green heart-shaped gummies beside the bottle. Preserve true gummy shape and finish from the reference.

cards.script: For women on a GLP-1,
cards.label: Warm eye-level portrait of the same woman at the kitchen counter, now looking ahead rather than down.

cards.script: the goal isn’t just another trip to the bathroom.
cards.label: Wide doorway view of her ordinary bathroom; she is in the adjacent hall, fully clothed. Do not show a bowel movement or imply verified relief.

cards.script: It’s feeling regular again—and getting on with your day.
cards.label: Close view of her picking up her bag and house keys from the hall table.

cards.script: Imagine waking up, going comfortably,
cards.label: Morning light on the same woman sitting up in bed; cut to a neutral bathroom-door detail. Editor label: IMAGINE YOUR MORNING.

cards.script: and getting dressed without wondering how long it’s been.
cards.label: She puts on a light cardigan over her usual tee and takes her bag. No altered waist size, flatter-stomach comparison or jeans transformation.

cards.script: Making plans without your stomach being the first thing you think about.
cards.label: Over-shoulder view of her choosing a time for coffee with a friend; hard cut to her picking up keys. Any phone text is added in the editor, not generated.

cards.script: You want to feel like yourself again,
cards.label: Eye-level exterior portrait just outside the same home; natural small smile, relaxed shoulders and warm daylight.

cards.script: without giving up the progress you’ve worked for.
cards.label: She walks out toward her day carrying her bag. No scale, body-size before/after or claims that medication effects are unchanged.

cards.script: Motilli. 90-day money-back guarantee. Tap below.
cards.label: Verified current bottle and exactly two dark-green heart-shaped gummies on cream stone. Editor-set brand, 90-DAY MONEY-BACK GUARANTEE and SHOP MOTILLI. Add a two-second silent tail.
